name: ConsignCare
domain: Medical-device consignment: case usage to billing, inventory and procurement

features.name: Case & Usage Capture
features.description: Turning what was used in surgery into a recorded, stock-deducted case — by photo, by scan or by hand.

features.name: Quotation & Hospital PO
features.description: Pricing the usage, getting it approved, sending it, and chasing the hospital's purchase order.

features.name: Stock & Procurement
features.description: Refilling hospital consignment stock, buying from suppliers, and knowing what is where and when it expires.

features.name: Billing
features.description: Invoicing the hospital against its PO and closing the case once paid.

features.name: Access & Insight
features.description: Who can see which hospitals, the dashboards, and the master data everything else reads.

actors.name: Sales Representative
actors.description: Owns a set of hospital accounts. Attends cases in the OR and records what was used, from a phone.

actors.name: Sales Admin
actors.description: Back-office. Prices usage into quotations, records hospital POs and raises requisitions.

actors.name: Sales Manager
actors.description: Approves quotations over the discount limit, requisitions and purchase requests. Watches the pipeline.

actors.name: Warehouse Officer
actors.description: Issues and receives stock, keeps lots and expiry dates honest, refills hospital consignment.

actors.name: Purchasing Officer
actors.description: Turns approved purchase requests into supplier POs.

actors.name: Accountant
actors.description: Invoices the hospital against its PO, records payment and closes the case.

actors.name: System Admin
actors.description: Keeps hospitals, doctors, products, contract prices and user access up to date.

actors.name: Hospital Purchasing
actors.description: The hospital's purchasing department: receives quotations and invoices, issues POs, pays.

actors.name: Supplier
actors.description: Manufacturer or importer the distributor buys from.

actors.name: OCR Service
actors.description: Vision model that reads usage sheets and sticker labels into structured items.

actors.name: LINE Messaging
actors.description: LINE Official Account used to send documents to hospital groups and alerts to reps.

actors.name: Email Service
actors.description: Transactional email for quotations, invoices and supplier POs.

actors.name: SSO Provider
actors.description: Company identity provider (Microsoft Entra ID / Google Workspace).

swim-case.title: A case, from surgery to cash
swim-case.summary: Everything before the rep confirms the items sits in DRAFT; the moment usage is confirmed the hospital's consignment stock is already gone, so every row after it is money the company is owed and the dashboard counts it.

swim-restock.title: Keeping the shelves full
swim-restock.summary: The warehouse finds the gap before a surgery does: search, expiry watch and the reorder point all lead to one purchase request, and nothing is in stock again until the goods receipt captures a lot and an expiry date.

steps.label: Trace where a lot was used

swim-onboard.title: Opening a new hospital account
swim-onboard.summary: A hospital is not usable until three things exist: the account, its contract prices and a rep assigned to it — the rep sees nothing until the last one is saved.

swim-quote.title: A quotation's life
swim-quote.summary: A quotation only waits on a person twice — the manager when the discount is over 10%, and the hospital for its PO; everything else is generated, rendered and sent by the system.

steps.label: Back with the admin to rework

swim-req.title: A requisition, from request to shelf
swim-req.summary: Approval is the only wait; once approved, the warehouse picks the earliest-expiring lots and the hospital's consignment is refilled in the same step.

swim-invoice.title: An invoice, until it's paid
swim-invoice.summary: An invoice leaves ISSUED one of three ways — paid, disputed, or overdue — and only the clock moves it to OVERDUE, which is why a scheduler is part of the stack.

swim-photo.title: A usage photo, read by AI
swim-photo.summary: The rep's only work is the photo and the confirmation; between them the photo moves through UPLOADED and PROCESSING on its own, and an unreadable one fails fast so the rep can retake it while still in the OR.

stack.name: TypeScript
stack.rationale: One language across PWA, web, API and worker; shared types for DTOs and state enums.

stack.name: Next.js
stack.rationale: App Router for both the rep PWA and the back-office; server components keep the back-office fast on hospital Wi-Fi.
stack.constraints: PWA install + camera via getUserMedia; iOS Safari ≥ 16.

stack.name: Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui
stack.rationale: Matches the navy/blue card look of the concept quickly; accessible primitives.
stack.constraints: Design tokens live in one CSS file.

stack.name: NestJS
stack.rationale: Modules map one-to-one to the bounded areas; DI makes ports and adapters natural.
stack.constraints: One deployable; modules may not import each other's repositories.

stack.name: Prisma
stack.constraints: Status CHECK constraints generated from stage 4.

stack.name: PostgreSQL
stack.rationale: Transactions across case, stock and quotation; row-level security option for hospital assignment.

stack.name: BullMQ on Redis
stack.rationale: Retries with backoff for OCR and notifications; delayed jobs for expiry and overdue.

stack.name: BullMQ repeatable jobs
stack.rationale: Clock-driven transitions: quotation expiry after 30 days, invoice overdue on due date, nightly reorder suggestions and expiry watch.
stack.constraints: Jobs are idempotent; one scheduler leader.

stack.name: Amazon S3
stack.rationale: Cheap, private storage for photos and PDFs; signed URLs.

stack.name: Claude vision (claude-opus-5-5)
stack.rationale: Reads the printed text under each barcode (REF LOT SERIAL) and the patient stickers into JSON with structured outputs; works on photos too small to decode barcodes from. Server-side fallback on refusal.
stack.constraints: Needs HN/AN to split cases, so the patient sticker is sent; the prompt and schema never return names or birth dates; provider under a DPA with no training on the data.

stack.name: zxing-wasm (multi-barcode, on device)
stack.rationale: Decodes every Code128 / DataMatrix sticker in a clear photo on the phone, offline, and splits them into patients by row gaps; also the live scanner.
stack.constraints: Needs ≥ ~2 px per bar: sheets photographed whole on a phone often fall below that, which is why AI reading of the printed text is the primary path.

stack.name: ZXing (GS1 DataMatrix / Code128)
stack.rationale: Decodes GTIN, lot and expiry from the GS1 barcodes on device packaging, in the browser.
stack.constraints: Needs camera permission; falls back to manual search.

stack.name: Playwright Chromium + exceljs
stack.rationale: HTML templates in Thai (Sarabun) give pixel-exact quotations and PRs; Excel export for PRs.

stack.name: Auth.js with Microsoft Entra ID / Google
stack.rationale: Company SSO plus email/password for small partners; JWT carries role and hospital ids.
stack.constraints: Hospital assignment enforced in the API, never only in the UI.

stack.name: LINE Messaging API + Amazon SES
stack.rationale: Thai hospitals live in LINE groups; email for formal documents.
stack.constraints: LINE OA verified; SES domain verified (DKIM).

stack.name: AWS ECS Fargate (ap-southeast-7)
stack.rationale: Bangkok region keeps personal data in Thailand; no servers to patch.
stack.constraints: Three services: api, worker, docs; web/PWA on the same cluster behind CloudFront.

stack.name: GitHub Actions
stack.rationale: Build, test, scan and deploy on merge.
stack.constraints: Production deploy needs a person's approval.

stack.name: OpenTelemetry + Grafana Cloud + Sentry
stack.rationale: Traces across API → queue → worker; front-end errors.

stack.name: Vitest + Playwright
stack.rationale: Unit and component in Vitest; E2E journeys in Playwright on mobile and desktop viewports.
stack.constraints: Test names carry Truss derived ids.

approach.rationale: One distributor, one small team, one database of record. A single deployable keeps the case → cash chain in one transaction where it matters (usage confirm + stock OUT; PO + quotation accept). Modules per area — cases, sales, supply, billing, identity — keep the option to split later. Ports keep the OCR model, LINE, email and the PDF engine replaceable.

patterns.name: State Machine
patterns.rationale: Case, quotation, requisition, purchase request, invoice and photo lifecycles are drawn at stage 4; the API refuses any transition the diagram lacks.

patterns.name: Repository
patterns.rationale: One per aggregate (case, quotation, requisition, PR, invoice) so rules never see SQL.

patterns.name: Adapter
patterns.rationale: OCR, LINE, email and document rendering sit behind ports the domain owns.

patterns.name: Outbox
patterns.rationale: A sent quotation or issued invoice and its notification job are written in one transaction, so nothing is sent for a rollback and nothing is lost on a crash.

patterns.name: Strategy
patterns.rationale: Notification channel (email, LINE) chosen per hospital at send time.

outcomes.pain: Reps re-type what was used from a photographed usage sheet, about 15 minutes a case, often at night.
outcomes.outcome: Usage is captured in the OR, from the photo they already take, in under 3 minutes.
outcomes.metric: Median minutes from case start to USAGE_RECORDED
outcomes.evidence: Concept brief (Capture usage by photo or scan); to validate with 3 reps over 40 cases in the pilot.

outcomes.pain: Used consignment items are never billed because a case gets lost between LINE chats, Excel and paper.
outcomes.outcome: Every used item reaches an invoice, and anything stuck is visible.
outcomes.metric: % of used-item value invoiced within 60 days
outcomes.evidence: Stock counts at hospitals regularly show more used than billed; to quantify from last year's consignment reconciliation.

outcomes.pain: Cash arrives weeks after the surgery because each hand-off waits for someone to notice.
outcomes.outcome: The quotation goes out the day usage is recorded and the invoice the day stock is issued.
outcomes.metric: Days from USAGE_RECORDED to invoice issued
outcomes.evidence: Sample of 30 closed cases from last quarter (to pull from accounting).

outcomes.pain: Consignment lots expire unnoticed on hospital shelves and are written off.
outcomes.outcome: Every lot's location and expiry is known; rotation is planned 90 days ahead.
outcomes.metric: Expired write-off as % of consignment value per year

outcomes.pain: Managers phone reps to find out where a case stands.
outcomes.outcome: Status of every case and hospital is on one dashboard, filtered to what each person may see.
outcomes.metric: Status questions answered without a phone call
outcomes.evidence: Manager interview (concept: One Team. One Platform.).

nfrTests.measure: Time from POST /photos to EXTRACTED, over a day of production traffic.
evidence: uc-ocr is async through the job queue

nfrTests.title: Back-office pages feel instant
nfrTests.requirement: 95% of API reads complete in under 400 ms at 50 concurrent users.
nfrTests.measure: k6 load test against staging with production-sized data (100k cases).
evidence: dashboard counts cases by status per hospital

nfrTests.title: Up when surgeries happen
nfrTests.requirement: Monthly availability of 99.5% between 06:00 and 22:00 ICT.
nfrTests.measure: Synthetic check on /health and sign-in every minute.
evidence: reps record cases in the OR

nfrTests.title: No lost photos in the basement OR
nfrTests.requirement: A photo taken offline is uploaded automatically within 1 minute of reconnecting, with zero loss.
nfrTests.measure: Playwright with network throttled to offline, then online.
evidence: Sales Rep App is a PWA

nfrTests.title: Reps see only their hospitals
nfrTests.requirement: Every case, quotation and stock read is filtered by hospital assignment server-side.
nfrTests.measure: Automated test per endpoint with a rep from another hospital.

nfrTests.title: Patient identifiers under PDPA
nfrTests.requirement: patient_hn and patient_an are encrypted at rest, masked in lists and never logged; the OCR step may read the patient sticker but returns and stores no name or date of birth; purged 5 years after case close.
nfrTests.measure: Log scan + DB column check + OCR response schema inspection.
nfrTests.threshold: 0 names or birth dates stored; 0 HN/AN in logs

nfrTests.title: Document numbers have no gaps
nfrTests.requirement: Quotation, invoice and PR numbers are sequential per year with no gaps or duplicates, as the Revenue Department expects.

nfrTests.title: Stock adds up
nfrTests.requirement: For every lot and location, the sum of movements equals the balance.

nfrTests.title: Readable on a phone in gloves
nfrTests.requirement: Touch targets at least 44 px; text contrast WCAG 2.2 AA; works at 200% zoom.

nfrTests.title: Room for the whole company
nfrTests.requirement: Holds 200 users, 60 hospitals and 250k cases (5 years) with no change to p95 targets.
nfrTests.measure: Load test on a staging copy seeded to 5-year volume.
evidence: 24 entities; stock ledger grows with every case

nfrTests.title: Metered services have a ceiling
nfrTests.requirement: OCR and email spend stays under ฿10,000 a month at 3,000 cases/month; alert at 80%.
nfrTests.measure: Monthly billing export vs. case count.
evidence: OCR Service and Email Service are metered and external

nfrTests.title: Every case can be traced
nfrTests.requirement: A trace id links the API request, queue job and worker call for every OCR and notification.
